issues.description: The solution implementation defines getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) (takes a boolean parameter), but the problem statement and UML specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() with no parameters. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected method signature and return behavior (whether guests are included by default), and prevents direct comparison between student implementations and the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem specification by changing the solution method to public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() with no parameters (returning the total number of students, including guests if that is the intended default). If the boolean option to include guests is desired, either add an overloaded method getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) in addition to the no-arg method, or update the problem statement and UML to document and require the boolean parameter.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a parameterless method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This changes the method signature for the same conceptual operation (retrieving the total number of students) and forces call sites (e.g. getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents) to pass a boolean. Students following the exercise instructions will look for a parameterless getTotalNumberOfStudents() as specified in the task/UML and may be confused when the provided solution/template uses a different signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution to provide the expected parameterless method signature: public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents. If a variant that excludes guests is desired, add an overloaded method (e.g. getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests)) but keep the parameterless version to match the problem/UML.
